1.30.m: with sacrificial grains, O best of gods, in which there is no violence, / having stayed for a maximum time of three years so that they do not sprout.

1.30.s:
eṣa dharmo mahāprājña virañcivihitaḥ purā /
evaṃ viśvabhugindrastu ṛṣibhistattvadarśibhiḥ //
1.30.d:
एष धर्मो महाप्राज्ञ विरञ्चिविहितः पुरा ।
एवं विश्वभुगिन्द्रस्तु ऋषिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
1.30.m: This is righteousness, O highly wise one, ordained by Brahmā of old." / Thus [was addressed] Indra, Viśvabhuj, by the seers who perceived the truth.

1.30.s:
tadā vivādaḥ sumahānindrasyāsīnmaharṣibhiḥ /
jaṅgamasthāvaraiḥ kairhi yaṣṭavyamiti cocyate //
1.30.d:
तदा विवादः सुमहानिन्द्रस्यासीन्महर्षिभिः ।
जङ्गमस्थावरैः कैर्हि यष्टव्यमिति चोच्यते ॥
1.30.m: Then there arose a very great dispute between Indra and the great sages: / "With what should one sacrifice—with mobile or immobile [offerings]?"

1.30.s:
te tu khinnā vivādena tattvamuttvā maharṣayaḥ /
sandhāya vākyamindreṇa papracchuḥ khecaraṃ vasum //
1.30.d:
ते तु खिन्ना विवादेन तत्त्वमुत्त्वा महर्षयः ।
सन्धाय वाक्यमिन्द्रेण पप्रच्छुः खेचरं वसुम् ॥
1.30.m: Exhausted by the dispute, having spoken the truth, the great sages, / making an agreement with Indra, questioned Vasu, who roamed the sky:

1.30.s:
sahāprājña kathaṃ dṛṣṭastvayā yajñavidhirnṛpa /
auttānapāde prabrūhi saṃśayaṃ no nuda prabho //
1.30.d:
सहाप्राज्ञ कथं दृष्टस्त्वया यज्ञविधिर्नृप ।
औत्तानपादे प्रब्रूहि संशयं नो नुद प्रभो ॥
1.30.m: "O highly wise one, how was the sacrificial rule seen by you, O king? / Speak, O son of Uttānapāda; dispel our doubt, O lord!"

1.30.s:
śrutvā vākyaṃ vasusteṣāma vicārya balābalam /
vedaśāstramanusmṛtya yajñatattvamuvāca ha //
1.30.d:
श्रुत्वा वाक्यं वसुस्तेषाम विचार्य बलाबलम् ।
वेदशास्त्रमनुस्मृत्य यज्ञतत्त्वमुवाच ह ॥
1.30.m: Hearing their words, without weighing the relative strength, / Vasu, recollecting the Vedic scripture, declared the truth of the sacrifice:

1.30.s:
yathopanīrtairyaṣṭavyamiti hovāca pārthivaḥ /
yaṣṭavyaṃ paśubhirme dhyairatha bījaiḥ phalairapi //
1.30.d:
यथोपनीर्तैर्यष्टव्यमिति होवाच पार्थिवः ।
यष्टव्यं पशुभिर्मे ध्यैरथ बीजैः फलैरपि ॥
1.30.m: "One should sacrifice according to what is brought near," said the king; / "one should sacrifice with sacrificial beasts, or else with grains and fruits.

1.30.s:
hiṃsāsvabhāvo yajñasya iti me darśanāgamau /
yatheha devatā mantrā hiṃsāliṅgā maharṣibhiḥ //
1.30.d:
हिंसास्वभावो यज्ञस्य इति मे दर्शनागमौ ।
यथेह देवता मन्त्रा हिंसालिङ्गा महर्षिभिः ॥
1.30.m: The nature of sacrifice is violent; this is my perception and scriptural tradition, / since the deities and the mantras here possess the marks of violence, according to the great sages,

1.30.s:
dīrgheṇa tapasā yuktairdarśanaistārakādibhiḥ /
tatprāmāṇyānmayā coktaṃ tasmātsa prāptumarhatha //
1.30.d:
दीर्घेण तपसा युक्तैर्दर्शनैस्तारकादिभिः ।
तत्प्रामाण्यान्मया चोक्तं तस्मात्स प्राप्तुमर्हथ ॥
1.30.m: who were endowed with long asceticism and perceptions such as [the wisdom of] the stars and so forth; / through their authority, I have spoken, and therefore you ought to accept it.

1.30.s:
yadi pramāṇaṃ tānyeva mantravākyāni vai dvijāḥ /
tathā pravatatāṃ yajño hyanyathā vo 'nṛtaṃ vacaḥ //
1.30.d:
यदि प्रमाणं तान्येव मन्त्रवाक्यानि वै द्विजाः ।
तथा प्रवततां यज्ञो ह्यन्यथा वो ऽनृतं वचः ॥
1.30.m: If those very statements of the mantras are authoritative, O twice-born, / let the sacrifice proceed accordingly; otherwise your word is false."

1.30.s:
evaṃ kṛtottarāste vai yuktātmānastapodhanāḥ /
avaśyabhāvitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tamatho vāgyatābhavan //
1.30.d:
एवं कृतोत्तरास्ते वै युक्तात्मानस्तपोधनाः ।
अवश्यभावितं दृष्ट्वा तमथो वाग्यताभवन् ॥
1.30.m: Being thus answered, those self-controlled ascetics, / seeing what was inevitable, then restrained their speech.

1.30.s:
ityuktamātre nṛpatiḥ praviveśa rasātalam /
ūrdhvacārī vasurbhūtvā rasātalacaro 'bhavat //
1.30.d:
इत्युक्तमात्रे नृपतिः प्रविवेश रसातलम् ।
ऊर्ध्वचारी वसुर्भूत्वा रसातलचरो ऽभवत् ॥
1.30.m: As soon as this was spoken, the king entered the netherworld; / though having moved in the heights, Vasu became a dweller of the netherworld.

1.30.s:
vasudhā talavāsī tu tena vākyena so 'bhavat /
dharmāṇāṃ saṃśayacchettā rājā vasuradhogataḥ //
1.30.d:
वसुधा तलवासी तु तेन वाक्येन सो ऽभवत् ।
धर्माणां संशयच्छेत्ता राजा वसुरधोगतः ॥
1.30.m: By virtue of that word, he became a resident beneath the surface of the earth; / King Vasu, the resolver of doubts regarding duties, fell downward.

1.30.s:
tasmānna vācyamekena bahujñenāpi saṃśaye /
bahudvārasya dharmasya sūkṣmā dūratarā gatiḥ //
1.30.d:
तस्मान्न वाच्यमेकेन बहुज्ञेनापि संशये ।
बहुद्वारस्य धर्मस्य सूक्ष्मा दूरतरा गतिः ॥
1.30.m: Therefore, even by one of much knowledge, [a judgment] must not be spoken alone in case of a doubt; / the course of righteousness, which has many doors, is subtle and very remote.

1.30.s:
tasmānna niścayādvaktuṃ dharmaḥ śakyastu kenacit /
devānṛṣīnupādāya svāyaṃbhuvamṛte manum //
1.30.d:
तस्मान्न निश्चयाद्वक्तुं धर्मः शक्यस्तु केनचित् ।
देवानृषीनुपादाय स्वायंभुवमृते मनुम् ॥
1.30.m: Therefore, no one is able to pronounce righteousness with absolute certainty, / taking into account gods and sages, except for Manu Svāyambhuva.

1.30.s:
tasmādahiṃsā dharmasya dvāramuktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ /
ṛṣikoṭisahasrāṇi svatapobhirdivaṃ yayuḥ //
1.30.d:
तस्मादहिंसा धर्मस्य द्वारमुक्तं महर्षिभिः ।
ऋषिकोटिसहस्राणि स्वतपोभिर्दिवं ययुः ॥
1.30.m: Therefore non-violence is declared by the great sages to be the gate of righteousness; / thousands of tens of millions of sages have gone to heaven by their own asceticism.

1.30.s:
tasmānna dānaṃ yajñaṃ vā praśaṃsaṃti maharṣayaḥ /
uñchamūlaphalaṃ śākamudapātraṃ tapodhanāḥ //
1.30.d:
तस्मान्न दानं यज्ञं वा प्रशंसंति महर्षयः ।
उञ्छमूलफलं शाकमुदपात्रं तपोधनाः ॥
1.30.m: Therefore the great sages do not praise giving or sacrifice; / ascetics [content with] gleanings, roots, fruits, herbs, and a pot of water,

1.30.s:
etaddatvā vibhavataḥ svarge loke pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
adrohaścāpya lobhaśca tapo bhutadayā damaḥ //
1.30.d:
एतद्दत्वा विभवतः स्वर्गे लोके प्रतिष्ठिताः ।
अद्रोहश्चाप्य लोभश्च तपो भुतदया दमः ॥
1.30.m: having given this according to their ability, are established in the heavenly world. / Absence of malice, absence of greed, asceticism, compassion for beings, self-restraint,

1.30.s:
brahmacaryaṃ tathā satyamanukrośaḥ kṣamā dhṛtiḥ /
sanātanasya dharmasya mūlametaddurāsadam //
1.30.d:
ब्रह्मचर्यं तथा सत्यमनुक्रोशः क्षमा धृतिः ।
सनातनस्य धर्मस्य मूलमेतद्दुरासदम् ॥
1.30.m: chastity, truth, sympathy, patience, and steadfastness— / this is the unassailable root of the eternal righteousness.

1.30.s:
śrūyante hi tapaḥsiddhā brahmakṣatrādayo 'naghāḥ /
priyavratottānapādau dhruvo medhātithirvasuḥ //
1.30.d:
श्रूयन्ते हि तपःसिद्धा ब्रह्मक्षत्रादयो ऽनघाः ।
प्रियव्रतोत्तानपादौ ध्रुवो मेधातिथिर्वसुः ॥
1.30.m: For sinless Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and others are heard of as perfected through asceticism: / Priyavrata, Uttānapāda, Dhruva, Medhātithi, Vasu,

1.30.s:
sudhāmā virajāścaiva śaṅkhaḥ pāṇḍyaja eva ca /
prājīnabarhiḥ parjanyo havirdhānādayo nṛpaḥ //
1.30.d:
सुधामा विरजाश्चैव शङ्खः पाण्ड्यज एव च ।
प्राजीनबर्हिः पर्जन्यो हविर्धानादयो नृपः ॥
1.30.m: Sudhāman, Virajas, Śaṅkha, the son of Pāṇḍya, / Prācīnabarhis, Parjanya, and kings such as Havirdhāna.

1.30.s:
ete cānye ca bahavaḥ svaistapobhirdivaṃ gatāḥ /
rājarṣayo mahāsattvā yeṣāṃ kīrttiḥ pratiṣṭhitā //
1.30.d:
एते चान्ये च बहवः स्वैस्तपोभिर्दिवं गताः ।
राजर्षयो महासत्त्वा येषां कीर्त्तिः प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
1.30.m: These and many other royal sages of noble nature / have gone to heaven through their own austerities, and their fame is established.

1.30.s:
tasmādviśiṣyate yajñāttapaḥ sarvaistu kāraṇaḥ /
brahmaṇā tapasā sṛṣṭaṃ jagadviśvamidaṃ purā //
1.30.d:
तस्माद्विशिष्यते यज्ञात्तपः सर्वैस्तु कारणः ।
ब्रह्मणा तपसा सृष्टं जगद्विश्वमिदं पुरा ॥
1.30.m: Therefore asceticism is superior to sacrifice by all reasons; / by asceticism this whole world was created by Brahmā of old.

1.30.s:
tasmānnānveti tadyajñastapomūlamidaṃ smṛtam /
dravyamantrātmako yajñastapastvanaśanātmakam //
1.30.d:
तस्मान्नान्वेति तद्यज्ञस्तपोमूलमिदं स्मृतम् ।
द्रव्यमन्त्रात्मको यज्ञस्तपस्त्वनशनात्मकम् ॥
1.30.m: Therefore sacrifice does not equal that; this [universe] is remembered as rooted in asceticism; / sacrifice consists of materials and mantras, whereas asceticism consists of fasting.

1.30.s:
yajñena devānāpnoti vairājaṃ tapasā punaḥ /
brāhmaṃ tu karma saṃnyāsādvairāgyātprakṛterjayam //
1.30.d:
यज्ञेन देवानाप्नोति वैराजं तपसा पुनः ।
ब्राह्मं तु कर्म संन्यासाद्वैराग्यात्प्रकृतेर्जयम् ॥
1.30.m: Through sacrifice one attains the gods, but through asceticism the Vairāja state; / through renunciation of action, the realm of Brahmā; through dispassion, mastery over material nature;

1.30.s:
jñānātprāpnoti kaivalyaṃ pañcaitāgatayaḥ smṛtāḥ /
evaṃ vivādaḥ sumahānya jñasyāsītpravarttane //
1.30.d:
ज्ञानात्प्राप्नोति कैवल्यं पञ्चैतागतयः स्मृताः ।
एवं विवादः सुमहान्य ज्ञस्यासीत्प्रवर्त्तने ॥
1.30.m: through knowledge one attains isolation: these are remembered as the five destinations. / Thus there was a great dispute at the inauguration of the sacrifice

1.30.s:
devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca pūrva svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare /
tatastamṛṣayo dṛṣṭvā hataṃ dharmabalena tu //
1.30.d:
देवतानामृषीणां च पूर्व स्वायंभुवे ऽन्तरे ।
ततस्तमृषयो दृष्ट्वा हतं धर्मबलेन तु ॥
1.30.m: between the deities and the sages in the earlier Svāyambhuva manvantara. / Then the sages, seeing him struck down by the power of righteousness,

1.30.s:
vasorvākyamanā dṛtya jagamuḥ sarve yathāgatam /
gateṣu munisaṃgheṣu devā yajñaṃ samāpnuvan //
1.30.d:
वसोर्वाक्यमना दृत्य जगमुः सर्वे यथागतम् ।
गतेषु मुनिसंघेषु देवा यज्ञं समाप्नुवन् ॥
1.30.m: disregarding Vasu's word, all went away as they had come. / When the hosts of sages had departed, the gods completed the sacrifice.

1.30.s:
yajñapravarttanaṃ hyevamāsītsvāyaṃbhuve 'ntare /
tataḥ prabhṛti yajño 'yaṃ yugaiḥ saha vivarttitaḥ //
iti śrībrahmāṇḍe mahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte pūrvabhāge dvitīye 'nuṣaṅgapāde yajñapravarttanaṃ nāma triśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.30.d:
यज्ञप्रवर्त्तनं ह्येवमासीत्स्वायंभुवे ऽन्तरे ।
ततः प्रभृति यज्ञो ऽयं युगैः सह विवर्त्तितः ॥
इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डे महापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते पूर्वभागे द्वितीये ऽनुषङ्गपादे यज्ञप्रवर्त्तनं नाम त्रिशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
1.30.m:
Thus indeed was the institution of the sacrifice in the Svāyambhuva manvantara; / from that time forward, this sacrifice has evolved along with the yugas.

Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, named “The Instituting of Sacrifice”, in the second Anuṣaṅgapāda of the first part in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa composed by Brahmāṇḍa and proclaimed by Vāyu.
